newsitem.title: CHINA: Construction to start on Siemens China power JV.
newsitem.headline: Construction to start on Siemens China power JV.

text.p: Construction of a 6.8 billion yuan ($819 million) Sino-foreign joint venture power plant in China's eastern province of Shandong is expected to begin soon, the China News Service said on Friday.
The first phase construction of the Rizhao power plant would include two 350-megawatt coal-fired generators, the agency said. It would have generating capacity of 2,500 megawatts.
Germany's Siemens AG and an unidentified Israeli firm would each hold a 12.5 percent stake in the power plant, the agency said.
Five Chinese firms, including Shandong Huaneng Power Development Co and state-owned China Power Investment Co Ltd, would hold the remaining 75 percent, it said.
The terms of cooperation would be 20 years, including a construction period of three-and-a-half years, the agency said but gave no further details.
It would be the first international fund-raising project without the guarantee of the government or financial institutions, it said.
